name: Question 12
problem:
$$
{y}^{″}+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x){y}^{′}+Q(x)y=0,\,x>0
$$

Let ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}$ be solutions to the second-order homogeneous differential equation above, where $Q(x)$ is continuous on $(0,\infty ).$ The Wronskian satisfies $W(\pi )=0.$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below.The Wronskian $W(x)$ satisfies the following first-order differential equation:

$$
{W}^{′}(x)={{field-1}}W(x)
$$

Solving this equation, we get

$$
W={{field-2}}
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.
